source_evidence:
Traditional IRA. Contributions typically are tax-deductible. You pay no taxes on IRA earnings until retirement, when withdrawals are taxed as income.
Roth IRA. Contributions are not tax-deductible but are made with after-tax dollars. Income earned on the account, from interest, dividends or capital gains, and withdrawals are generally tax-free.
question: How do the tax treatments of Traditional and Roth IRAs differ?
answer: Traditional IRA contributions are typically tax-deductible, and taxes on earnings are deferred until retirement; withdrawals are then taxed as income. Roth IRA contributions are made with after-tax dollars and are not tax-deductible, while account earnings and withdrawals are generally tax-free.
